cells.tense: The heart is open here, and nothing has been poured in yet.
cells.act: let yourself be drawn before you choose
cells.ask: Before a call you'd normally make quickly, lean for a moment first. Notice which way you lean before you decide the lean is allowed.
cells.core:
The heart is open here, and that's new. Before there's a name for what's stirring, you can feel it moving — several directions possible at once, none of them settled yet. That's not vagueness. It's the part that comes before picking, and you're sitting inside it without bracing against it.

That openness doesn't demand an answer yet. The pull of what might be felt can run for a minute before your will closes over it. Then set down one plain thing: what drew you, before you'd agreed to be drawn. Write it where you'll find it later, not because it's conclusive, but because the leaf is turning and you can tell it's happening. The open heart and the deciding hand can share the same minute.

cells.tense: The open heart is already deciding what it will feel, long before there's anything to feel.
cells.act: complete the form so it stands without you
cells.ask: Pick a decision you keep rehearsing the ending of, set the moment to finish it, and stand there when it's done — stop adding to it.
cells.core:
The openness is running ahead of itself, and it's doing that here, where you choose. The heart is open, so it grabs at futures: what the other will say, how the choice will look, what it proves about you. The vessel is so busy reaching forward that the present hasn't been poured in yet, and the direction you actually want keeps getting buried under directions you've braced against.

Try finishing it. Take the decision you keep rehearsing and give it a real close — a date, a sentence, a settled answer. Finish it, then don't revise it the next day. The finishing is what will teach you where your will actually lives, in what can be seen, not in what might yet be felt. Less to hold, and the present has something poured into it at last.

cells.tense: The heart opened somewhere, and you have been standing at that door ever since.
cells.act: carry what the spark became to its full size
cells.ask: Take the thing you once stepped toward and give it one size more. Name it plainly, then say what it would look like held at that size rather than the smaller one you've kept.
cells.core:
Something opened once. You can tell, because nothing since has quite had that reach. What you felt then is still what you felt then — the door it walked through has closed, and the rest of life has been sized to the door, not the feeling. Direction is quiet here. There is movement, but it's the movement of not going further.

Start small, back at the beginning. Take one thing that once pushed at you, and this week meet it as it is now — not the old version, this one. Carry what it became, not what it promised to be, and hold it at the size it's actually reached. You don't have to feel anything about that. You just pick it back up where you actually left it.

cells.tense: You have been choosing for other people so long that deciding looks like something everyone does.
cells.act: let the exchange with someone run both ways
cells.ask: When someone hands you something real — a favour, a hand, an introduction — take it once without squaring the ledger. See what receiving is like.
cells.core:
This is running, and you don't count it as yours. You've been the one who picks, who takes what's offered and makes it land, through the whole stretch where direction was needed. Somewhere in that you started giving other people credit for a direction that comes from you, and the version of the story where this is your work keeps being handed to someone else.

Refuse one of those handoffs. Let one exchange with another person run fair straight through: you give what you gave, and let what you didn't give come back in full, without shrinking it or returning it. The direction was yours before there was a story about whose direction it was. You can start keeping what you allowed someone else to call theirs.
